title: How big is the universe?
examples: Teacher, how far away is the edge of the universe?
Can you show us how big the universe is compared to Earth?
What is the biggest thing we can see in space?

explain.say: We start by looking at our own planet Earth.
Next, we look at our solar system, which includes the Sun.
Our solar system is part of a galaxy called the Milky Way.
Galaxies are huge groups of billions of stars together.
The observable universe is the giant bubble we can see around us.
To show the scale, the observable universe is incredibly vast.

faq.q: How far away is the edge of the universe?
faq.a: We do not know if the universe actually has an edge. The observable universe is just how far we can see light from.
asks: Does the universe have a boundary?
What limits our view of space?

faq.q: Is the Milky Way the only galaxy out there?
faq.a: No, there are billions of galaxies in the observable universe. Our galaxy is just one of many.
asks: Are there other galaxies besides ours?

faq.q: How do scientists measure such huge distances?
faq.a: They use things like measuring the light from distant stars. Light takes time to travel across space.

faq.q: Does the universe have a center?
faq.a: Scientists do not think the universe has a center. Everything is expanding outwards from everywhere.
asks: Is there a middle point in space?
Is the expansion happening from one spot?

faq.q: What is the difference between a galaxy and the universe?
faq.a: A galaxy is a collection of stars. The universe is everything, including all the galaxies.
asks: Are galaxies part of the universe?
What is the biggest structure in space?

facts: Our solar system is located within the Milky Way galaxy.
The Milky Way is a spiral galaxy containing billions of stars.
The observable universe is the region of space from which light has reached us.
Galaxies are vast collections of stars, gas, and dust.

quiz.say: What structure contains our solar system?
quiz.why: The Milky Way is the name of the galaxy our solar system belongs to.

wrong.0: Andromeda is a neighboring galaxy, but it is not the galaxy we are in.
wrong.2: This is too big; it describes everything we can see, not just our neighborhood.
wrong.3: The solar system is only the Sun and planets, not the whole galaxy.

quiz.say: What is the main component of a galaxy?
quiz.why: Galaxies are made up of billions of stars, along with gas and dust.

wrong.0: While important, stars are the visible, primary components we learn about first.
wrong.1: Vacuum is empty space; galaxies are full of matter.
wrong.3: Planets orbit stars; they are not the main component of a whole galaxy.

quiz.say: If we see light from a distant galaxy, what does that tell us?

options.show: How long ago the light left
options.say: How long ago the light left

options.show: How much energy the galaxy has
options.say: How much energy the galaxy has

quiz.why: Because light takes time to travel, seeing it tells us how long ago it started its journey.

wrong.1: Speed is related, but the light travel time gives us the age/distance measurement.
wrong.2: Energy is related to mass, but light travel time is the direct measurement tool.
wrong.3: Galaxies are physical objects, not living things that can be 'alive'.
